title: Advance Quarterly Services Report (Third Quarter 2026) — Census's named AIES benchmark release for services, 10:00 a.m. ET
source: CENSUS: two independent census.gov primaries fetched direct 2026-09-06 by this event's own initial research, both naming the date. (1) economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html (HTTP 200, 91,396 bytes, 179 table rows parsed), row "Advance Services Report | November 19, 2026 | 10:00 AM | Third Quarter 2026", release code A202611191000, reference A202603. (2) services/release_schedule.html, the QSS program's OWN schedule table headed "2025/2026 Release Schedule for the Advance Quarterly Services Report and the Quarterly Services Report — All releases occur at 10 am", whose "2026 Quarter 3" row reads "Thursday, November 19, 2026" for the advance and "Thursday, December 10, 2026" for the full report; the same table's "2025 Quarter 3" row reads "Suspended | Thursday, December 11, 2025". Corroborating third: services/index.html's Announcements block names this exact release — "Effective with the November 2026 advance release for the third quarter of 2026, we anticipate that not seasonally adjusted quarterly services estimates will be revised to reflect historical corrections and results of the 2023 and 2024 Annual Integrated Economic Survey." Promoted estimate -> confirmed and EST: -> CENSUS: on the two-primary precedent this calendar already carries for housing-starts-2026-12-17, m3-full-report-2026-12-03 and durable-goods-2026-11-25. Confirmed is a statement about the SCHEDULED DATE, not about publication risk: this series carries a Suspended row 12 months back and the ledger states that separately. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: Canonical file written by this id's own initial research (2026-09-06) after reading its one proposal, `from-wholesale-trade-2026-11-09`, which is now shadowed. Three findings correct or sharpen it. (1) WHAT THIS PRINT IS: not primarily "the resumption test" the proposal framed, but Census's NAMED AIES benchmark release for the services series — services/index.html names the November 2026 advance release for Q3 2026 as the edition carrying the 2023+2024 Annual Integrated Economic Survey results, historical corrections, and new seasonal factors for the seasonally adjusted Selected Services Total. That is the services-sector twin of the 2026-10-26 wholesale restatement, carried inside a regular release rather than as a standalone event. (2) THE SUSPENSION RULE IS SUPPORTED AND MEASURABLY COSTLESS ON THIS SERIES. Census's own program schedule prints the pattern in one table: Q3 2025 advance "Suspended", Q3 2025 full report "Thursday, December 11, 2025" — and CB25-162 published that full report on that date, on time, $6,119.4B +2.4% (+/-0.4). The funding lapse deleted the 21-day preview and zero data. Contrast the Advance Economic Indicators Report, which lost FIVE editions (Sep/Oct/Nov 2025, Jan/Feb 2026); this series lost exactly one and resumed at its very next slot (CB26-34, 2026-02-20). (3) THE PROPOSAL'S "CENSUS DATA-ENTRY ODDITY" IS REFUTED: reference code A202603 is the standard A<yyyy><qq> quarterly form, consistent across all 28 scheduled rows 2020-2026 (A202004 = Q4 2020 ... A202603 = Q3 2026), including the suspended A202503 = Q3 2025. Impact LOW and symbols empty on measured grounds, not assumption: across 1,871 GDPNow vintages 2014-05-01 -> 2026-07-28, the Quarterly Services Survey is named ZERO times, and the Atlanta Fed's forward PostedUpdates calendar posts no vintage on 2026-11-19 or on the paired 2026-12-10 full report; no house playbook is macro- or services-keyed (re-grepped 2026-09-06, 0 hits in trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md); on 22 realized release sessions since 2021 the S&P 500's median absolute close-to-close move is 0.339% against a 0.561% baseline, permutation p=0.157 — a null, not an edge. Date confirmed; nothing here licenses an entry.
